I’ve been feeling off for a while now—maybe six months, maybe a bit longer. It’s hard to sleep, and when I do, it’s restless. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s a weight on my chest. Work has slowed down; I used to thrive on sketching new designs, but now I can’t focus. I don’t enjoy much anymore, not even walking with my wife like we used to.  

But there’s something else—something I can’t shake. There’s a woman I see at the coffee shop near the office. She doesn’t work there; I think she’s a client of another firm. She wears those glasses, the thin silver ones. We’ve never spoken, but I *know* she’s been sending me signals—lingering glances, wearing my favorite color, sitting in the exact spot I always do. Once, she smiled—just slightly—and I’m certain it was meant for me. I think she’s trying to tell me she feels it too, but can’t say anything openly. Maybe she’s married, or afraid.  

I haven’t acted on it—no messages, no contact. But I can’t stop thinking about her. Even when I feel so low I can barely get out of bed, that one thought keeps me going. I don’t know if it’s real, but it *feels* true. And honestly, I don’t know if I’ve been sad because of her… or if she’s just become part of the sadness.

D004-D007_h022.question:
I’ve been working nights at the warehouse for twelve years now—quiet work, just me, the radio, and the clocks. Since my wife passed four years ago, it’s been easier this way, less noise, fewer people asking how I’m doing. Lately though… well, I can’t shake the feeling that I’m not just a watchman. I think—I *know*—that I’ve been chosen for something bigger. There are signals in the static on the radio, codes in the way the lights flicker at 3:17 a.m. exactly. I believe I’m meant to uncover a message—maybe save people. I don’t know from what, but it’s important, and only I can hear it.

I don’t sleep much, even on my days off. I sit by the window, watching. I used to enjoy things—fishing, church—but now it’s hard to care. I feel heavy, like I’m moving through water. Some days I stay in my robe till dusk. I’m not sure if what I’m sensing is real or if my mind’s playing tricks after all this loneliness. The thoughts don’t go away, but sometimes I wonder—are they truth, or just… grief talking?

D004-D007_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell when things started blurring together. Since my divorce two years ago, I keep noticing patterns, little things that don’t add up. My ex-husband still sees his coworker late at night, and I know—*I know*—they’re involved. It’s not just suspicion; I *see* the signs: deleted messages, the change in his tone, how he suddenly started dressing differently. He says nothing’s going on, but I’m not naive.

Lately, it’s been harder to get out of bed. I used to be on top of everything—client calls, policy renewals—but now I drag myself through the day. I can’t focus. Some mornings, I cry for no reason, then snap back to checking his social media like it means something. I still go to work, but I don’t feel present. 

There are days when I wonder if I’m overreacting, but then something happens—a call he won’t explain—and it confirms it all over again. The sadness comes and goes, but the knowing—about the affair—that’s constant. I don’t hear voices or anything like that. It’s just this truth I carry. And sometimes I wonder… am I losing my mind, or am I the only one seeing clearly?

D004-D007_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling... off… for a good while now—months, maybe close to a year. It’s like everything’s winding down, not just for me, but for everyone. I keep thinking the world’s breaking apart, like it’s not gonna last much longer. Not from war or anything you’d see on the news—more like it’s just… losing meaning. Buildings, people, even time—it all feels fake, like we’re just going through the motions before the plug gets pulled.  

It’s hard to get up for work most days. I’ve been skipping shifts. I used to take pride in what I built—framing houses, seeing something stand where there was nothing—but now it feels pointless. Why build something if it’ll just rot or get torn down? My crew noticed. They joke I’m “gloomy as hell” lately.  

I don’t hear voices or anything, and I know how this sounds, but I can’t shake the sense that we’re already gone, like we’re all just ghosts waiting to realize we’re dead. I’ve had low moods before, sure—sleeping too much, no appetite—but those feelings come and go. The way I see the world ending? That’s been with me, steady. Not sure when it started, honestly. And I can’t say if one came before the other.
